title: Fast Acknowledge, Repair, and Automated Status Payloads
author: Sofia R. Kim
body:
Summary:
This runbook defines the Fast Acknowledge & Restore (FAR) workflow for short-duration, high-customer-impact incidents ("blips") and provides automated status-page payload templates and customer communication scripts. It is intended for first responders and incident commanders to recover service quickly, maintain consistent customer messaging, and capture the minimal data needed for follow-up triage or a postmortem if impact persists.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to recovery (MTTR) for incidents that are expected to be resolved within 60 minutes.
- Scope: Applies to all 3rd-line engineering oncall, SRE, and the oncall rotation owners for Redwood production services (examples: inference-gateway, model-router, kv-cache, batcher). Not for security incidents — escalate to Security runbook in that case.

Quick facts (SLOs and thresholds):
- Availability SLO (global): 99.95% uptime per calendar month (service-level target for production inference API routes).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile tail < 300ms for small requests, 99th percentile < 1.5s for standard generate endpoints.
- Error budget -> action thresholds: 40% of budget used => engineering review; 100% => immediate rollbacks and postmortem.
- Impact classification (use for communications):
  1) Minor blip: <10% customer requests affected, corrective action < 15m; low comms
  2) Service blip: 10–50% affected OR degradation > 15m; status page update required
  3) Outage: >50% affected OR customer-visible SLA breach; exec escalation and customer emails

Roles & responsibilities:
- First responder: acknowledge on PagerDuty, start FAR workflow, update status page (initial) within 5 minutes.
- Incident Commander (IC): assigned if >20m or impact rises category; coordinates cross-team work and customer comms.
- SRE lead: owns runbook correctness and post-incident follow-up.
- Product/CS liaison: prepares customer-facing summaries for enterprise customers if Outage.

FAR workflow (fast path for blips):
1) Acknowledge (0–5 minutes):
   - Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty.
   - Post brief note to #ops-incident Slack channel: "ACK: {service} {signal} — working on it (first responder: @me)."
   - Identify service (check tags in alert): inference-gateway | model-router | kv-cache | batcher.
2) Quick triage (5–12 minutes):
   - Check health endpoints and metrics:
     - curl -sS https://prod.{region}.redwood.ai/{service}/health | jq
     - kubectl -n prod get pods -l app={service} -o wide
     - grafana dashboard: /d/redwood/{service}-overview
   - Look for recent deploys: git rev + timestamp from rollout annotation.
   - If traffic is saturated, check autoscaler: kubectl describe hpa {service}
3) Contain & repair (12–45 minutes): choose fastest safe fix.
   - If a bad deploy suspected: rollback to previous revision (helm/argo):
     - argo rollouts promote {service}-stable || helm rollback {release} {rev}
   - If pod crashloop / OOM: increase replicas temporarily or reduce concurrency: kubectl scale deploy/{service} --replicas=3
   - If kv-cache eviction hotspot: restart cache workers one-by-one and clear large keys with TTL: redis-cli -h {host} --csv KEYS "temp:*" | xargs -n 1 redis-cli DEL
   - If model-router overload: route traffic to fallback model via feature flag: curl -X POST https://flagmgr.redwood.internal/flags/route -d '{"service":"model-router","target":"fallback"}'
4) Verify & restore (45–60 minutes):
   - Run synthetic check: curl -sS https://prod.{region}.redwood.ai/health-check?scenario=smoke
   - Confirm metrics trend recovered: error-rate returning to baseline for 3 consecutive minutes.
   - Update PagerDuty/Slack with resolution summary.

When to escalate to full incident process (IC + bridge):
- Impact classification is Service blip and not resolved in 20 minutes.
- Any Outage condition (category 3).
- Cross-region or cross-service cascading failures.

Runbook snippets for common signals (examples):
- inference-gateway high 5xx:
  1. Check ingress error rates (alb/nginx) and downstream latency to model-router.
  2. If 5xx from upstream model-router, open model-router runbook.
  3. If errors originate at gateway, recycle gateway pods: kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-gateway -n prod
  4. If ingress shows high request spikes, temporarily enable rate-limit: curl -X POST https://ops.redwood.internal/rate-limits -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","limit":"50rps"}'

- model-router degraded routing:
  1. Check routing table: redis-cli -h router-cache GET routing:weights
  2. If missing entries, trigger config push: curl -X POST https://configmgr.redwood.internal/push -d '{"service":"model-router"}'
  3. If cold KV cache causing high latency, warm caches by running warmup job: kubectl create job -n prod warmup-model-router --from=cronjob/warmup-model-router

- kv-cache evictions & latency spike:
  1. Inspect memory and eviction metrics in CloudWatch/Prometheus.
  2. Temporarily increase node autoscaling or restart a bounded set of workers to avoid cascading restarts.
  3. If thundering herd from a specific key prefix, delete or TTL the keys and rehydrate with low-priority background jobs.

Automated status-page payloads (templates)
- Purpose: keep messages consistent and machine-driven for quick updates. Status service accepts JSON POSTs to /api/v1/incidents.
- Minimal initial payload (use within 5 minutes for Service blip):
  {
    "incident": {
      "id": "auto-{timestamp}-{service}",
      "service": "inference-api",
      "impact": "partial",
      "start_time": "{iso_timestamp}",
      "short_summary": "Increased error rates for inference API in {region} — engineers investigating",
      "next_update_est": "{+15m}"
    }
  }
- Progress update payload (use when verification step is complete):
  {
    "incident": {
      "id": "{id}",
      "status": "monitoring",
      "update": "Applied rollback to {service} deployment; error-rate trending down. Continuing to monitor."
    }
  }
- Resolved payload:
  {
    "incident": {
      "id": "{id}",
      "status": "resolved",
      "end_time": "{iso_timestamp}",
      "summary": "Root cause: bad model rollout (regression in preprocessor) — rolled back. No data exfiltration. Postmortem scheduled."
    }
  }

Command examples (curl):
- Create initial incident: curl -X POST https://status.redwood.internal/api/v1/incidents -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API' -d @initial.json
- Update incident: curl -X PATCH https://status.redwood.internal/api/v1/incidents/{id} -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API' -d @update.json

Customer communications templates
- Short status banner (status page & in-app):
  - Title: "Partial degradation of inference API in {region}"
  - Body: "We are investigating elevated error rates affecting a subset of requests. We have engineers working on a fix and expect an update within 15 minutes. If you rely on dedicated capacity, contact your CSM for an SLA update."
- Enterprise email (when Impact=Outage):
  Subject: "Redwood incident: inference API degraded in {region} — {start_time}"
  Body: "Hi {CustomerName},

  We are experiencing a degradation affecting inference requests in {region}. Our engineers have identified a model rollout as the likely cause and are taking steps to mitigate (rollback in progress). We will provide updates at least every 30 minutes until service is restored.

  Impact: {brief bullet list of impacted routes/services}
  Next update: {+30m}

  We apologize for the disruption. Your CS and support teams are on standby to assist with any urgent mitigations.

  Regards,
  Redwood Incident Response Team"

Post-incident minimal postmortem template (to be filled within 48h if event escalated):
- Title: Short Incident Postmortem — {service} — {date}
- People: responder(s), IC, reviewer(s)
- Timeline (HH:MM UTC): detection -> acknowledge -> mitigation -> verification -> resolved
- Root cause (concise):
- Actions (owner + due date):
  1) Add automated smoke test for deployment path (owner: infra-team — due: 2 weeks)
  2) Harden model rollout gating in CI (owner: model-onboarding — due: 1 week)
- Severity & customer impact summary
- Follow-up meeting time & attendees

Game day catalogue (quarterly cadence recommended):
- Scenario A: Canary regression during peak traffic (goal: detect rollback automation within 20m).
- Scenario B: Multi-region failover (goal: verify automated routing and status page for cross-region outage).
- Scenario C: Thundering herd on kv-cache after cache eviction (goal: validate TTL strategies and warmup jobs).
- Scenario D: Bad model weights causing high 5xx and latency (goal: exercise rollback and escalation to product).

For each scenario:
- Runbook owner, start time, detection trigger, expected remediation timeline, scoring metrics (MTTA & MTTR targets, customer-notification timeliness), and post-game retro checklist.

Runbook testing & maintenance:
- Runbook smoke test: monthly scheduled job where an oncall engineer reviews top 3 steps in this document and simulates the health checks (non-disruptive).
- Full game day: quarterly, rotate ownership across SRE, Serving Runtime, and Platform teams.
- Document updates: after every incident where FAR workflow used, first responder adds 1–2 line notes to this doc within 72 hours. SRE lead consolidates quarterly.

Appendix: quick-check cheat sheet (printable)
- Step 0: Acknowledge in PD + Slack (0–5m).
- Step 1: Health checks + pods + recent deploy (5–12m).
- Step 2: Fast mitigation (restart/rollback/scale/warm) (12–45m).
- Step 3: Verify, update status, close (45–60m).

How to update this page:
- Edit in Confluence space: oncall-and-incident-response -> fast-acknowledge-repair-and-automated-status-payloads-2026.
- Add reviewer and comment with test evidence after any change.

Ownership & contact list:
- SRE oncall alias: oncall-sre@redwood.ai
- Status API owner: #tooling-status (Slack) / owner: Aisha Thompson
- PagerDuty escalation policy: Redwood-Prod-P0 (see PagerDuty console for rotation)
